title: The Asset of Geneva
premise: Zephyrine Thornbury, a discreet interpreter for a doomed Geneva peace delegation, has spent years erasing himself from every record — until the safe house he lives in appears on a real estate site, its interior photographed down to his coded notebooks. The listing is a message: someone inside the delegation knows who he is and what he buried in a previous life. As Zephyrine traces the leak through translators, couriers, and a broker with ties to Frankfurt finance, he uncovers a plot to stage the delegation's collapse as an accidental gas explosion timed to move markets at Monday's open. Forced to choose between protecting the found family of misfits who sheltered him and exposing a truth that will destroy one of them, he sabotages the attack and testifies anonymously, trading his invisibility for their survival. In the end, the safe house sells; Zephyrine keeps only the photographs of the people, not the place.
about_author: Silas Pemberton is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in cities that no longer exist on itineraries. He writes thrillers about the invisible professionals who keep negotiations from collapsing, and about the cost of being good at disappearing.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. During a fractious translation session, Zephyrine finds the safe house listed online — every room photographed, including his hidden notebook shelf. He realizes someone with access took the photos. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a man whose entire identity rests on not being seen, suddenly exposed. He begins quietly cataloguing who entered the house in the past month.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Ever Knocked
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Zephyrine and Mara, the safe house's young caretaker who becomes his reluctant ally. They trace the photographer's metadata to a courier tied to delegation security — and find a second set of documents: an 'accident' scheduled for Sunday night, before Frankfurt opens. Emotional beat: wary trust hardening into loyalty as Mara chooses him over her employers.

chapters.title: The Price of Glass
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, climax. At the delegation's final gala, Zephyrine identifies the traitor — the mentor who once gave him his new name, selling the delegation's failure to short-sellers. To stop the gas release beneath the venue, Zephyrine must publicly break cover, using his linguistic skills to expose coded instructions mid-interpretation. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made literal; he burns his old life to save the room.

chapters.title: What the Photographs Keep
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, resolution. The explosion never comes; markets open flat; the mentor vanishes rather than face trial. The safe house sells, and the makeshift family scatters — but Mara finds Zephyrine left each of them a photograph and a false name they can use if they ever need help. Emotional beat: bittersweet inheritance; invisibility surrendered, connection kept. Final image: a new listing, empty rooms, no people in them.
